pr.title: Add field uninstall: the installer's uninstall target removes what the installer made (install.md §3.5)
pr.head: 9b9357d8d39da39080c2f62f89e719b276d6332a

summary: Field installs in one of two ways. A release install is what curl -fsSL https://field.one/install.sh | bash makes: the installer, install.sh, downloads a release's source into a directory of its own under ~/.local/share/field, builds it there, and puts a two-line script, the shim, at ~/.local/bin/field to run it. A checkout install is a clone that pnpm's global field links to. Before this change, removing a release install meant an rm -rf from the docs, and removing a checkout install meant knowing to run pnpm remove -g field.

This change adds an uninstall target to install.sh, and a field uninstall command that runs it the way field upgrade runs the installer. In a release install, the target removes only what the installer can show it made, by the same tests the installer already uses to prune old versions, and it keeps everything else with a kept row. In a checkout install, it removes pnpm's link only when that link points at this checkout, and it never deletes the checkout.

The new head fixes both earlier findings. A release shim is removed only when it points at the data directory being removed; another installation’s shim stays with a row naming its directory. Model-weight output now names ACE-Step’s own directory and Chatterbox’s Hugging Face cache separately, for the workers that were set up.
The field.one uninstaller has shipped in okamnesiac/audiofield#43. Until a release carries this target, it runs 0.3.0’s installer, which rejects uninstall with exit status 64 and changes nothing.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Data directory (DATA_DIR): where release installs live. It is FIELD_DATA_DIR when set, otherwise $XDG_DATA_HOME/field or ~/.local/share/field.
  • Bin directory (BIN_DIR): where the shim goes. It is FIELD_BIN_DIR, then what release.conf recorded, then ~/.local/bin.
  • Version: a directory named X.Y.Z holding one built release. The installer counts it as its own only when it is a real directory, not a symlink, whose install.sh carries SHIM_MARKER, the comment line every shim starts with.
  • Download: .download-X.Y.Z, the staging directory a release unpacks in, counted only when it holds unpacked/.
  • current: the symlink naming the version the shim runs.
  • release.conf: the repository, ref, and bin directory the install follows.
  • Fetch cache: cache/fetchcontent, JUCE's download, which every version's daemon build shares.
  • prune: the installer step that removes old versions after an upgrade, using the same two tests.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The review of ef4ef2e requested changes on two P2 findings. Both are fixed and their resolved threads are verified at 9b9357d. The full gpt-6 review at this head is clean, with no open finding thread.
  • The new installer cases cover another installation’s shim, an unreadable exec line, a data-directory alias with a quoted path, per-worker weight rows, and cache overrides.
  • pnpm typecheck, all 110 focused tests, project check, and bash -n install.sh pass.
  • The install plan stays in-progress. Its earlier domain question predates this change.

groups.title: The installer's uninstall target
groups.kicker: install.sh learns to remove what it installed, and nothing else
intro: install.sh already had five targets: all, cli, audiod, workers, and status. It runs each one in one of two modes. When the script sits in a git work tree beside src/cli.ts, it is a checkout installer. Otherwise, piped from curl or downloaded by field upgrade, it is a release installer. This group adds uninstall to both modes.

In release mode, uninstall_release has to work in a data directory that may hold other things, because FIELD_DATA_DIR can point anywhere. So it removes a directory only when the installer can show it made it. A version is a real X.Y.Z directory whose install.sh carries SHIM_MARKER. A download is .download-X.Y.Z with unpacked/ inside. Both tests are the ones prune uses after an upgrade. The shim is removed only when its quoted exec path identifies this data directory; directory aliases compare by file identity. Another install’s shim is kept with its data directory named. The owned shim goes first, so field never runs a version that is half removed. The target then removes current, release.conf, and JUCE's download, and removes the data directory only if it is empty.
In checkout mode, uninstall_checkout runs pnpm remove -g field only when pnpm's global field links this checkout, and it always leaves the checkout itself.

files.note: Adds release and checkout uninstall targets, checks the data directory a release shim runs, and reports each worker’s own weights directory.

checks.text: shim_runs_here reads the quoted path without evaluating it and checks text equality or directory identity. The focused tests cover a different install, an unreadable exec line, and a quoted path through a directory alias.
Version and download removals still use the installer’s existing ownership tests; foreign files survive in the focused tests.
ACE-Step’s row uses FIELD_ACE_MODELS or ~/.field/models/acestep, matching models_root. The tests confirm its weights remain and only configured workers receive rows.
Chatterbox’s row respects HF_HUB_CACHE ahead of HF_HOME. The override test confirms both workers’ output names their configured directories.

groups.title: field uninstall, the command
groups.kicker: A doorway to the installer's target, found the way field upgrade finds it
intro: field upgrade already runs the right installer for the install it runs from. A checkout runs its own install.sh. A release install downloads the newest installer for the repository and ref in release.conf into a temporary directory, and tells it where the data directory is with FIELD_DATA_DIR. With FIELD_OFFLINE set, a release install runs the installed version's own copy instead.
uninstall() refuses on Windows with a message naming pnpm remove -g field, then calls upgrade('uninstall'), so the command shares all of that. Its exit status is the installer's.

files.note: Adds uninstall(): a Windows refusal, then upgrade('uninstall', deps).

checks.text: The earlier review exercised uninstall through a release shim both offline and with an installer downloaded through a local file URL. This command delegates to the same installer path that upgrade already uses.
Errors raised inside upgrade() still say cannot upgrade: … when you ran field uninstall, such as a failed download. The review lists this as a suggestion.

files.note: Registers field uninstall and sets process.exitCode to what the installer returned.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: The real installer under bash against stand-ins, and the command's handoff
intro: src/install.test.ts runs the real install.sh with bash, against a temporary HOME and a PATH that holds only stand-ins for pnpm, cmake, curl, and the field CLI, plus links to ordinary tools. Nothing installed on the machine can answer in their place. This change adds rmdir to those tools, a remove -g branch to the pnpm stand-in, and an install.sh uninstall block that also covers the two ownership and cache-location fixes.
src/commands/upgrade.test.ts checks that field uninstall hands a stand-in installer the uninstall target and returns its exit status, and that it refuses on Windows.

groups.title: The plan: §3.5 and its decision
groups.kicker: The install plan records the uninstall design and why a separate script lost
intro: The install plan gains §3.5, "Uninstall", with what the target removes and keeps in each mode, and how field.one/uninstall.sh will run it. §4 records the decision that uninstall is a target of the one installer. A separate uninstall.sh in this repository, and a TypeScript-only field uninstall, lost because each would need its own copy of the data directory's resolution and of the ownership tests. §5 adds criteria, §6 marks chunks 3 and 4 shipped and adds this one as chunk 5, and §10.3 records the first real install from GitHub. The updated §3.5 names both workers’ weight directories and requires a shim to run this data directory. It also records that the field.one uninstaller shipped before the release.
The plan stays in-progress, and this change opens no question. §7.4, on which domain serves the installer, is still open from before this change, although chunk 4 shipped field.one.

groups.title: User docs
groups.kicker: Uninstall instructions, and field.one as the install URL
intro: docs/install.md replaces the manual rm -rf and pnpm remove -g field with field uninstall, and adds the target to both target tables. The README, docs/install.md, and docs/cli.md lead with curl -fsSL https://field.one/install.sh | bash. docs/release.md's example bumps patch, since releases are patch bumps from here on.

checks.text: Curl uninstall needs the same FIELD_DATA_DIR used for installation. Without it, the installer keeps a shim for a different data directory and tells you which one.
The output preserves both model caches. ACE-Step’s directory is shared by Field installs; Chatterbox uses a Hugging Face cache shared by other tools.
